sections.h2: What is on file at the Sampson County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Sampson County calls its Register of Deeds the official custodian of records for county residents, keeping a permanent, standardized record of who owns real estate and how it changed hands. The office files deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and miscellaneous real estate papers.

Vital records share the same counter: birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharges, and the commission records of notaries public. The office also swears in notaries.

The county site points to online access for these records. Start there for the index search before you phone anyone, and write down the book and page of each deed you find. A homeowner who inherited a Sampson County house can trace each recorded deed back through the chain of owners and confirm every name is spelled the same way, which saves trouble when a title company runs its search.

sections.h2: Will the Sampson County office explain how to fill out a deed?
sections.html:
No. Per the county, this is a recording office alone, and state law forbids the register of deeds and staff from practicing law. They will not provide legal forms, walk you through completing one, or comment on what a filed paper does legally.

That divides the work on a Sampson County sale:

  • An attorney drafts the deed and answers wording questions.
  • A title agent or closing attorney searches the chain of title and arranges loan payoffs.
  • The register of deeds checks each paper against recording rules, takes the charge, and indexes it.

When a house came to you through a family arrangement, see an attorney first. A recorder cannot repair a deed that was written wrongly.

Errors an attorney tends to catch include a misspelled seller name, a missing preparer line on page one, and a land description at odds with the mapped parcel. Sorting those out before closing costs far less than a corrective deed afterward, and it keeps your buyer's lender from pausing the funding.

sections.h2: What does Sampson County charge on a deed filing?
sections.html:
Section 161-10 sets the schedule the register applies, and the statute treats it as the whole list. Payment comes first, so request a combined total when several papers go in together.

After closing, request a certified copy of the recorded deed, because lenders, heirs and later buyers tend to ask for it.

sections.h2: Who pays excise tax on a Sampson County deed?
sections.html:
Sellers pay. A deed conveying an interest in land carries a levy of $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, with a partial $500 block counted whole, and the transferor remits it to the recorder ahead of filing (section 105-228.30).

One half goes to Sampson County's general fund. The rest flows to the state, after refunds and a small collection allowance. For land in more than one county, the county with the greater value collects.

Check that the tax shows on its own line of your closing statement, so your net proceeds are no surprise. If you split costs with the buyer by contract, put the allocation in writing, since the statute assigns the tax to the transferor by default.

sections.h2: How does recording order protect a Sampson County buyer?
sections.html:
Section 47-18 ties a deed, option, first refusal right or lease over three years to the moment of registration: until then it does not bind lien creditors or later buyers who paid value. Order of registration sets rank. That is why closing instructions usually call for same-day filing, and why delay can cost a buyer first position.

Filing the buyer's deed and the new lender's deed of trust together gives that buyer first position. For the seller, a recorded cancellation of the old mortgage clears the index. Forgotten, uncancelled liens can resurface and slow a later sale.

sections.h2: What happens to a Sampson County parcel with unpaid property tax?
sections.html:
Section 105-355 makes unpaid tax a lien as of the listing date, together with penalties, interest and costs. The county may pursue it through a court action patterned on a mortgage foreclosure (section 105-374).

If it comes to that, the parcel is auctioned at the courthouse door. The sale is reported within three days, exceptions or a raised bid can be filed for ten days after that, and anyone redeeming before confirmation pays the tax along with penalties, interest and costs.

sections.h2: Which other Sampson County tools help a seller around recording?
sections.html:
The county runs several web tools next to the recorder's index, each useful before listing:

  • The GIS Data Viewer searches by owner name, address or parcel ID and shows property layers, maps and reports.
  • The Property Record Search draws on the Tax Department's database for the parcel.
  • The Tax Bills site lets you search, view and pay a bill.
  • The Development Services Portal covers building inspection, planning and zoning and environmental health, with permit applications and status checks.

Use the GIS viewer to confirm the parcel ID and acreage match your deed. Check the permit portal for open permits or unfinished work tied to the address, which an inspector for the buyer could uncover.

The county also states that it handles public record requests under Chapter 132 of the General Statutes. Anything the register keeps is public, so assume anyone, a title examiner included, can read what you recorded.

sections.h2: Which Sampson County towns bill tax on a sale?
sections.html:
The county tax office collects for the county, fire and school districts and, at present, for the municipalities of Clinton, Autryville, Harrells, Newton Grove, Salemburg, Turkey and Garland. The address is PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329, and the phone is (910) 592-8146.

The office says county bills fall due on September 1, and it allows a 2 percent discount for payment by August 31, and that parcels still unpaid are listed in a newspaper notice, normally early in April. Your closing attorney needs the current balance for the parcel before anything is sent to the recorder, so request it as soon as you have a contract.

faqs.q: Can the Sampson County Register of Deeds give legal advice about a deed?
faqs.a: No. As the county puts it, the office exists to record documents, and the law bars staff from practicing law. They cannot supply forms, explain how to complete them or discuss what a filing means.

faqs.q: What excise tax applies to a Sampson County deed?
faqs.a: It is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, paid by the transferor ahead of filing under section 105-228.30. The county general fund gets half, and the state gets the rest.

faqs.q: What is the standard filing charge in Sampson County?
faqs.a: Under section 161-10, $26.00 covers an ordinary instrument through page 15, with $4.00 for every page past that. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through page 35. Cancelling one costs nothing. A certified copy is $5.00, plus $2.00 for each extra page.

faqs.q: What else does the Sampson County office handle?
faqs.a: Birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharges and notary records, plus notary oaths, according to the county site.

faqs.q: Why file a deed promptly after closing in Sampson County?
faqs.a: Registration fixes priority. Under section 47-18, a conveyance binds lien creditors and later buyers for value only from registration, so quick filing protects the buyer's position.
